full_judgment:
9. The learned Additional District Magistrate, Chittagong considering the facts and circumstances of the case and evidence on record by his judgment and order dated 28.06.1993 convicted the accused petitioner no. I Nizamuddin and petitioner No.2 Abdur Roaf under section 324 of the Penal Code sentencing them thereunder to suffer rigorous imprisonment for two years and also convicted petitioner No.3 Mostafizur Rahman and two others under section 223 of the Penal Code sentencing them thereunder to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 9 months and awarded tine of taka 1000/- in default to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 3 (three) months and others accused were acquitted by him. 

 10. Being aggrieved by the judgment and order of conviction and sentence dated 28.06.1993 passed by the learned Additional District Magistrate, Chittagong the accused petitioner preferred Criminal Appeal No. 93 of 1993 before the learned Sessions Judge. Chittagong who transferred the case to the learned Additional Sessions Judge, 4th Court. Chittagong for hearing and disposal. The learned Additional Sessions Judge, 4th Court. Chittagong on consideration of the facts and circumstances of the case and evidence on record by his judgment and order dated 30.03.2002 dismissed the appeal affirmed the judgment and order dated 28.06.1993 passed by the learned additional District Magistrate, Chittagong, in CR Case No. 36 of 1986. 

 Mr. Faroque Ahmed the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the accused petitioners took me through the complainant, evidence of 4 (four) witnesses the impugned judgment and order of the conviction and sentence dated 30.03.2002 of the learned Additional sessions Judge as well as the judgment and order of the learned Additional District Magistrate Chittagong and submits that the judgment and order of conviction and sentence passed by the learned courts below are perfunctory, based on conjecture, surmise, hypothesis which suffer from non-reading and misreading of evidence. He further submits that admittedly there has been enmity between the complainant and accused persons over landed property and other criminal matters. It is further stated that there has been a civil case No. 111 of 1976 and CR. Case No 85 of 1983 between the complainant and accused party and the complainant party was convicted in CR case No. 85/85. The complainant has instituted the instant case falsely in order to take revenge of that conviction. He further submits that both the courts below erred in not appreciating the evidence properly and the learned Courts below failed to consider that there was strong enmity between the parties which led the complainant to file the case on false grounds. 

 13. Mr. Faroque Ahmed the learned further, Advocate submits that complainant has ''examined 4 witnesses P.W.1 Saiful Alam complainant is not eye witnesses P.W.2 Alauddin. P.W.3 Kamaluddin and P.W.4 Alamgir are alleged victim who are sons of the complainant and there is no independent and disinterested witnesses and there also no corroboration of the independent witness with the evidence of the complainant. He further submits: that the complainant stated in the petition that victims were under ' treatment in the health complex and the doctor 'lave two certificates in favour of their injury but the doctor has not been examined in order to prove the certificates given by the doctor and that without examining the doctor the certificates given by him will not be taken into evidence. It is further submitted that wearing apparels of alleged victims were not seized. neither the wearing apparels with blood stained mark of alleged victim nor any piece of blood stained earth were produced in the court as alamats to prove the case of prosecution which also attracts section 114 (g) of the evidence Act and lastly he submits that the judgment and order of conviction and sentence of both the courts below suffer from inherent infirmity and the learned Courts below erred in law in not finding that the prosecution failed to prove the case by producing neutral independent. disinterested and reliable witnesses to prove its case which caused Failure of justice and as such the impugned judgment and order dated 30.03.2002 passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge, 4th Court, Chittagong affirming the judgment and order of conviction and sentence dated 28.06.1993 passed by the learned Additional District Magistrate are liable to he set aside. 

 15. Mr. Mir Mahafizur Rahman the learned advocate for the opposite party No. 2 submits that the defence by examining 3 eye witnesses has proved the case narrated in the complaint. Ile further submits that since the eye witnesses by corroborating one another has proved the case, then there is no need for medical certificate and examination of doctor is also not necessary for-convicting the accused petitioners. lie also cited the case of Nowabul Alam and others vs. The State reported in 15 BLD(AD) (1995)54 where in their Lordships held that there is no rule of law that if independent witnesses are not available in a case a conviction cannot he sustained on the evidence of eye witnesses who are relative and partisan witnesses. If found to be trustworthy conviction can be based on the evidence of' such interested witnesses. He further referred the same case where in their Lordships held that When both the parties are equally powerful and divided in two hostile groups at the present day, nobody likes to involve himself' in group rivalry between two strong factions of people. In such a case it is indeed difficult for the prosecution to examine independent witnesses as the villagers would he reluctant to side with any of the parties who had longstanding enmity and rivalry between them. 

 18. It appears from the evidence of PW-I that there are about 2/3 hundred inhabitants in his village; that the house of Mollah Bari is 250/300 squire feet’s far from the place of occurrence where about 200 people reside. But none of the neighbor of that Mollah bari are also witness of this case. 

 19. P.W. 2 Alauddin also deposed that hearing his scream, Jabul, Liman and Humayun also came to the place of occurrence to save him but none of these persons were examined in this case. The persons of Mollah Bari and Jabul, Emran and Humayum are the most neutral and vital witnesses in this case who have not come to prove the case. None from the vicinity were examined as witnesses on behalf of the complainant. It appears from the submission of the learned Advocate for the petitioner that these witnesses were examined, they would not support the prosecution case rather they would support the defence case that is why they were withheld from examining in this case. Thus the case of the prosecution is hit by section 114(g) of the Evidence Act and the defence is entitled to get benefit of this section. There is substance in the argument of the learned Advocate for the accused petitioners. Both the courts below ought to have found that due to serious enmity between the parties and non-examination of independent and 'disinterested witnesses the impugned judgment cannot be sustained. 

 20. Both the courts below erred in law not deciding that the medical certificate cannot be taken into evidence as the doctor was not examined. It is also found that no alamats like wearing apparels of the victims with blood stained cloths were sized to prove the alleged occurrence by the prosecution. 

 21. On perusal of the evidence on record I am of the view that the judgment and Order of conviction and sentence dated 30.03.2002 passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge, 4th Court, Chittagong in criminal Appeal No. 93 of 1993 are not based on independent witnesses rather the impugned judgment and order is based on conjecture surmise hypothesis and that the impugned judgment is not well reasoned basing on the facts and circumstances of the case and 

 evidence on record and the judgment and order suffer from misreading and non-reading reading of the evidence which call for the interference by this court. I find merit in this rule which must be succeeded.
